description: An anatomical structure or region. Anatomy combines the multi-species Uberon anatomy ontology with the Allen Institute Human Brain Atlas ontology (HOMBA), which adds detailed human brain structures. A node may represent an Uberon term, a HOMBA structure, or corresponding concepts from both sources. Some distinct HOMBA structures share a single Uberon term and are represented together at that coarser anatomical granularity.

common_properties.name: identifier
common_properties.description: Anatomical term identifier as a full prefixed CURIE: an Uberon identifier (for example UBERON:0000002) or a HOMBA identifier (for example HOMBA:10155 or HOMBA:AA30004).

common_properties.name: name
common_properties.description: Canonical anatomical name from Uberon for Uberon-identified nodes, or the HOMBA structure name for HOMBA-identified nodes.

common_properties.name: sources
common_properties.description: Data sources contributing the anatomical concept: uberon, HOMBA, or both.

common_properties.name: last_updated
common_properties.description: When this node was created or its documented properties were last changed.

source_contributions.scope: Non-obsolete anatomical terms with an identifier and name from the Uberon basic anatomy ontology. Covers anatomy across species rather than human anatomy alone.
source_contributions.description: Uberon provides anatomical terms, canonical names, and optional text definitions. Its relationships describe anatomical subtypes and structural containment.

properties.name: def
properties.description: Text definition of the anatomical structure or region supplied by Uberon.
properties.notes: If absent in source, omit property

source_contributions.scope: Human brain structures from the Allen Institute Human Brain Atlas ontology, including structures with Developing Human Brain Atlas (DHBA) identifiers and HOMBA-only structures.
source_contributions.description: HOMBA supplies detailed human brain anatomy and a containment hierarchy of regions, areas, layers and nuclei. Corresponding concepts can carry both Uberon and HOMBA provenance. HOMBA and DHBA identifiers and names provide additional ways to identify and search for these structures. Several HOMBA structures can be represented by one Uberon concept.

properties.name: aliases
properties.description: Additional anatomical identifiers contributed by HOMBA. Uberon-identified nodes may carry HOMBA: and DHBA: CURIEs; HOMBA-identified nodes may carry a DHBA: CURIE.

properties.name: synonyms
properties.description: Alternative HOMBA and DHBA anatomical names. Names differ case-insensitively from the canonical name and other synonyms; historical names may also remain.
